method: Complete pinned SSE4.1 C source read with Git/SHA256 verification; no x86 runtime credit from prior ARM controls.
findings: Single-block compression performs seven explicit rounds, maintaining row1 unrotated and compensating message shuffles. In-place emits32 bytes; XOF emits64 with CV mixed into second half.

compress_pre reads all64 block bytes even when block_len is smaller. Caller must supply accessible padded block storage; block_len does not bound memory reads. Higher-level source was previously reviewed but no new unsafe-call failure claimed.

Vector hash_many processes four inputs with transposed message lanes and per-input counters;1..3 remaining inputs use this SSE compression individually. Unlike NEON, scalar-count remainder is still SSE accelerated.
32-bit counter carry uses unsigned comparison via sign-bit XOR, high-word subtract of all-ones mask. Boundary parity requires actual x86 execution or independently validated emulation.
Input/output use unaligned16-byte intrinsics; four-lane output ordering interleaves low/high halves into contiguous32-byte digests. No pixel or AST control can prove intrinsic lane correctness.
Start/end flags apply at first/last full block; counter remains same for blocks within one input and advances across inputs when requested. Zero-input call performs no output.
Message prefetch uses offset+256, and callers must satisfy complete-block data contract. No performance or memory-fault conclusion from prefetch syntax alone.
SSE4.1/SSSE3 intrinsics require correct dispatch and compiled feature flags. Separate x86 assembly implementations remain unread and do not inherit C-source review credit.
limits: No SSE compilation/execution, x86 ABI qualification or throughput measurement.
